hosts.note: Machines that registered with this node over POST /hosts, as they described themselves: CPUs, memory, GPUs and the sandboxes each can run jobs under. Summed over live hosts. Held in this process's memory, forgotten after a day, verified by nobody, and never a record -- a worker on one of these hosts is paid for what the log shows it submitted, not for being listed here.

compute.note: Every worker that has heartbeated to this node on any objective, from its own reports: the device is what the worker called itself, the class a heuristic over that name, and the rate the node's own measurement where it has one. Summed over live workers. Not a record, not verified, and not what anyone is paid for -- that is under `derived` on GET /progress/{id}.

hardware.note: This process's own machine, probed at startup. The node runs verifiers on it and nothing else; a worker's hardware is what the worker reports in its heartbeats, under `compute`.

known.duty: posts and funds objectives, accepts submissions, hands out work assignments and keeps the lease roster workers coordinate through
runs workers that take assignments, heartbeat, lease tasks and submit claims to this node
runs pinned verifiers and stands behind verdicts under bond, so a wrong verdict has somebody answerable
holds and serves the log and reconciles it with peers
known.evidence: nothing in the log; sessions on GET /sessions

sandbox.why: bwrap is installed but cannot create a namespace on this host

unservable.lean: 'lean' not on PATH; install a Lean toolchain to verify

note: Three kinds of fact, kept apart: `node` is what this process declares and can see of its own machine; `peers.reached` and `compute` are what peers and workers did and said recently, held in this process's memory and verified by nobody; `roles.evidenced` is recomputed from the log. Only the last is something a reader can check.

roles.note: Recomputed from this node's log: funders of objectives, submitters of accepted claims, attestors of verdicts. Roles here are what identities did, not titles they hold; a node's declared roles are under `node.roles` and are a hint.
